title: Performance Monitoring
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of performance monitoring and at least two listed subtopics.
Interpret the performance monitoring example and predict its expected result.
Choose a verification step and identify one version, security, data, or troubleshooting consideration.

content.intro: Learn performance monitoring through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Performance Monitoring matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines performance monitoring as part of performance, caching, and scalability. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Request timing; Query metrics; Cache hit rates; Error and saturation rates; Profilers and application monitoring tools. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Request timing
items.text: Request timing is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Query metrics
items.text: Query metrics should be evaluated using a representative workload and a measured baseline. Compare correctness and resource usage before and after the change; the best choice depends on the database backend, request mix and data size.

items.title: Cache hit rates
items.text: Cache invalidation and key scope are part of correctness. Include relevant variation dimensions, use a deliberate TTL, avoid cross-user leakage, and invalidate or refresh entries after writes.

items.title: Error and saturation rates
items.text: Treat Error and saturation rates as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

items.title: Profilers and application monitoring tools
items.text: Profilers and application monitoring tools should be evaluated using a representative workload and a measured baseline. Compare correctness and resource usage before and after the change; the best choice depends on the database backend, request mix and data size.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Request timing. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
